 Judgment

Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award by which the Tribunal directed respondent No.1/owner to pay the compensation, this appeal is filed by petitioners under Section 173(1) of MV Act (1988) with a prayer to enhance the compensation.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
3. Petitioners filed claim petition seeking compensation in a sum of Rs.13,00,000/- for the death of their son in a motor vehicles accident dated 23.12.2016.

4. It is the case of the petitioners that on 23.12.2016 at 15:15 hours, deceased was going on extreme end of road by walk, at that time, driver of Maruti Wagnor car bearing Reg.No.GA-03/P-0181 from opposite side in a negligent manner and dashed to deceased, which resulted in accident and deceased died on the spot.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Maruti Wagnor car belongs to respondent No.1 and insured with respondent No.2.
As owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, respondents are liable to pay the compensation.

5. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared and filed written statement, denying the age, occupation,
nature of injuries sustained and due to the injuries, deceased died. Respondent No.1 insured his car with respondent No.2 and policy issued is in force and respondent No.1 is not liable to pay any compensation.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. Respondent No.2 contended that the driver of the offending vehicle is not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle involved in the accident.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.
7. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
8. Petitioner has got examined himself as PW.1 and relied upon Exs.P1 to 6.

On behalf of respondents, respondent No.2 examined his official as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R1 to 4.
9.

Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal partly allowed the claim petition granting compensation in a sum of Rs.8,94,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum and directed respondent No.1/owner to pay the same.

The details of the compensation granted are as under:

10. Heard arguments and perused the records.
11.
During the course of argument, the learned counsel for the petitioners contended that the Tribunal has not properly considering the income of the deceased.
The Tribunal has granted meager compensation on all the heads, hence, requires enhancement.

12. To substantiate his arguments, learned counsel for the petitioners relied upon decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Jawahar Singh vs Bala Jain & Ors. reported in (2011) 6 SCC 425.

entities.text: Jawahar Singh vs Bala Jain & Ors. reported in (2011) 6 SCC 425
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, sought for allowing the appeal by enhancing the compensation.
13. Learned counsel for the respondent/insurance company contended that accident is not proximate cause to the death of the deceased.
Owner of the offending vehicle entrusted the vehicle to the driver with full knowledge who was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle involved in the accident.

14. In support of his argument, he relied on decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs Kaushalya Devi and others reported in 2008(8) SCC 246; another decision in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd., vs Rakesh Kumar Arora and others reported in 2008(13) SCC 298.
15.

sentences.text:
Since the accident is of the year 2016, the income ought to have been taken at Rs.8,750/- p.m.
instead of Rs.8,000/- p.m.
The deceased was aged 18 years, the appropriate multiplier would be 18.

However, the Tribunal has not added any compensation towards loss of future prospects as per Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1,
(Magma's case), 40% is required to be added towards loss of future prospects.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the income is required to be taken at Rs.12,250/-.
Since the deceased was bachelor 50% is required to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

With these components, the compensation under the head loss of dependency is Rs.12,250/- x 12 x 18 x 50% =
Rs.13,23,000/- against Rs.8,64,000/- granted by the Tribunal.
16. As parents, petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/- each i.e., (2018) 18 SCC 130 Rs.80,000/- under the head loss of love and affection.
Similarly, Rs.15,000/- granted by the Tribunal towards loss of funeral expenses is just and proper.

Thus, in all petitioners are entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.14,18,000/- as against Rs.8,94,000/- granted by the Tribunal as detailed below:
18.
Now coming to the question of liability.
The claim petition filed against respondent No.2 is dismissed only on the ground that the driver of the vehicle was not having licence at the time accident.
It is submitted that at the time of accident the driver was minor, but the Tribunal has not fastened the liability on insurance company.

It is an undisputed fact that as on the date of accident,
the offending vehicle was covered by a valid policy issued by respondent No.2.
However, the Tribunal has exonerated respondent No.2 from the liability on the ground that at the time of accident driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving licence.

However, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pappu & Ors vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba & Anr.2, it was held that when the offending vehicle is insured, in the absence of the driver of offending vehicle possessing a valid driving licence, the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner.

entities.text: Pappu & Ors vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba & Anr.2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in this case also it is necessary to direct respondent No.2/insurance company to pay the compensation with interest and recover the same from respondent No.1-owner.

19. To this extent, the appeal deserves to be allowed and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(2018) 3 SCC 208 (ii) Appellants/petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.14,18,000/-
as against Rs.8,94,000/- granted by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% per annum.

(iii) Respondent No.2/insurance company is directed to pay the compensation together with interest within a period of six weeks from the date of this order and recover the same from respondent No.1/owner.
(iv) The order of the Tribunal regarding apportionment, payment and deposit shall hold good for the enhanced compensation also.
(v) The registry is directed to send a copy of this order to the Tribunal.
